name: The Jasmine Minks
label: Creation Records
lede: An Aberdeen band mailed a demo to Melody Maker and ended up as Creation single No. 4, recorded for £50. McGee then sent them busking across London, eight gigs in a day, and signed them again seventeen years later.

eras.title: From Aberdeen to the Living Room
eras.text: Four Aberdonians sent a tape to a music paper and got Alan McGee instead. They were on Creation Records before the label had a hit, cutting singles in a cheap Waterloo studio and playing McGee's club.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks · The Jasmine Minks on Bandcamp · Creation Records: Jasmine Minks interview · Press and Journal
years.h: A demo to Melody Maker gets them a call from Alan McGee
years.p: Jim Shepherd and Adam Sanderson on guitars and vocals, Martin Keena on bass and Tom Reid on drums form the band in Aberdeen. McGee recruits them for his new label.
years.xp:
The demo was a four-track tape made at Jim Shepherd's place on Selhurst Road, and Melody Maker made it demo of the week. McGee rang. Shepherd remembers the first question: "Do you like the Velvet Underground?"

McGee sat in on rehearsals and told them to cut the songs down; 'Think!' ran about five minutes. There was no contract, just McGee managing them on trust. Years later he called them "the first real Creation band" and "working-class heroes."

The band's own Bandcamp calls them "the first band signed to Alan McGee's Creation records." Their first single was Creation's fourth.

q: We did twelve singles before I found the Jesus and Mary Chain
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks · Discogs: Think! · The Line of Best Fit
years.p: [[Joe Foster|6a850a84-6293-4788-9e05-ccd9fd4f0315]] produces CRE 004 in Waterloo, with Dave Musker adding keyboards. It's made a single of the week, alongside [[The Pastels|9d6108ad-dbc2-4bf1-a746-edc1044d2749]].
years.xp: McGee's line, from his autobiography, puts the Minks among the label's first run of singles, before [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]] made Creation's name. The Line of Best Fit later heard Creation's early mod fury in 'Think!'.

years.src: Discogs: Alive in the Living Room
years.h: Two covers on Alive in the Living Room
years.p: Creation's first LP, recorded live at McGee's club, has the Minks playing [[Love|34ec9a8d-c65b-48fd-bcdd-aad2f72fdb47]]'s 'Seven and Seven Is' and 'Green Fuz'.
years.xp: The album was taped at the Living Room between August 1983 and February 1984. The last track on it, by [[Television Personalities|62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c]], is cut short by a police raid on the club.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks · Discogs: Where the Traffic Goes · The Big Takeover
years.h: Eight gigs in one day, on acoustic guitars
years.p: To push 'Where the Traffic Goes', CRE 008, McGee sends the band on a one-day busking tour. Police move them on, pubs invite them in, and the day ends at the Living Room.
years.xp:
The acoustic sets ran through streets and pubs and wound up at the Rough Trade shop, before the electric gig at the Living Room that night.

The reviews were strong and the NME picked the Jasmine Minks as one of the eighteen most hopeful bands in Britain. The NME showcase that followed fell during a National Union of Journalists strike, and the band played to a very sparse audience.

The runout groove on the single's B-side asks: DOES ANYONE REMEMBER PUNK ROCK?

years.src: Discogs: One Two Three · Creation Records: Jasmine Minks interview
years.h: Six songs, a title longer than some of them
years.p: The mini-album, CRE LP 003, comes in red-and-black and yellow-and-black sleeves. Musker plays Hammond and Farfisa.
years.xp: Richey Edwards later wrote to the band to tell them the title had given the [[Manic Street Preachers|32efea44-6cb5-4b4f-bdaa-c8b8f6cef981]] their name, Shepherd said in 2001.

eras.title: Cold Heart, and a singer leaves
eras.text: The singles climbed the indie chart, the BBC asked for sessions, and the first full album was made back home in Aberdeenshire for a few hundred pounds. Then Adam Sanderson left.

years.cap: The Jasmine Minks in The Sun Shines Here fanzine, issue 1, 1985
years.src: Discogs: What's Happening · Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks
years.h: 'What's Happening' reaches No. 27 on the indie chart
years.p: Sanderson and Shepherd write CRE 018 together, with 'Black & Blue' on the flip.

years.h: On the bill the night the Mary Chain gig turns into a riot
years.p: The Minks play the North London Polytechnic show with [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]]. Shepherd: "a full scale riot developed."
years.xp: The Mary Chain had borrowed the Minks' gear to record 'Upside Down'. It hurt when McGee stopped managing the Minks to concentrate on the Mary Chain, Shepherd said in 2001, "but it was understandable."

years.p: The Minks record for [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s Radio 1 show. Precious Recordings issued it on EP in 2021.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks · Discogs: The Jasmine Minks
years.h: The first album is cut in Ellon for £600
years.p: The Jasmine Minks, CRELP 007, is recorded in Ellon, Aberdeenshire. 'Cold Heart' goes to No. 17 on the indie chart, the band's highest.
years.xp:
Someone scratched a sentence across the two runout grooves, starting "I think I see the tunnel" on side one and finishing "at the end of the light" on side two.

'Cold Heart' got a music video. Glass Modern reissued the album in 2022.

years.h: Adam Sanderson leaves, and Shepherd sings lead
years.p: After 'Cold Heart', Sanderson quits. Jim Shepherd takes over the vocals and keyboard player Paul Cooper joins.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks · The Jasmine Minks on Bandcamp
years.h: Back at the BBC for Janice Long
years.p: The new line-up records a Radio 1 session for Janice Long. Precious put it out in 2021.

eras.title: Organ up front
eras.text: With Shepherd singing and Cooper's organ in the middle, the Minks made two more albums for Creation, with a different second guitarist each time. After the second they stopped for most of a decade.

years.h: The Pure EP comes out on Esurient Communications
years.p: The band steps off Creation for one release in 1987.

years.src: Discogs: Another Age · Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks
years.h: Dave Arnold of the Claim fills in on Another Age
years.p: CRELP 025 is recorded at Alaska Studios, apart from 'Cut Me Deep', cut at Planet Studios in Edinburgh with Walter Duncan on guitar.

years.src: Discogs: Scratch the Surface · Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks · Backseat Mafia
yt: Live at the Falcon, Camden, March 3, 1989
years.h: Ed de Vlam plays guitar on Scratch the Surface, then the band stops
years.p: The band produces CRELP 044 at the Greenhouse in London with engineer Steve Nunn. De Vlam then moves to Spain, the band runs out of steam, and the Minks stop for about a decade.
years.xp:
Shepherd wrote about 30 songs for it and kept a dozen. "I was listening to Big Star non-stop and that comes across in the group sound," he said in 2021. De Vlam's playing leaned on Tom Verlaine.

It didn't sell much, and Shepherd felt the rushed mix let it down; the remaster later fixed the balance.

eras.title: McGee signs them twice
eras.text: The Minks came back as the Creation era was ending, and McGee put them on his next label. Reissues and old BBC sessions followed, and in 2023 a new album.

years.p: The comeback album comes out on Genius Move.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks · Discogs: Popartglory · Creation Records: Jasmine Minks interview
years.h: Alan McGee signs them again, this time to Poptones
years.p: Popartglory and the single 'Daddy Dog' come out on McGee's post-Creation label.
years.xp: Shepherd wrote the new songs with guitarist Wattie Duncan, swapping parts by email. [[Joe Foster|6a850a84-6293-4788-9e05-ccd9fd4f0315]], who had produced 'Think!' in 1984, pushed for the record at Poptones.

years.cap: The Jasmine Minks at the Borderline, London
years.src: Discogs: Cut Me Deep · Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks
yt: Cold Heart live at the Borderline, July 2011
years.p: Cherry Red's Cut Me Deep runs from the Creation singles to the reunion records.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jasmine Minks · Discogs: We Make Our Own History · Press and Journal · The Big Takeover · Jangle Pop Hub
years.h: We Make Our Own History, on red and blue vinyl
years.p: The first full-length Minks studio album in 23 years is a co-release by Last Night from Glasgow and Spinout Nuggets, with Shepherd and Wattie Duncan up front.
years.xp:
The singles 'Step by Step' and 'Gravity' came out in 2019, when the band told The Big Takeover a new album was due in 2020. It took until late 2023.

Jangle Pop Hub's verdict: "Still essential, grab your vinyl LP."
